title: Implement byt website sync command
description:
Add command to sync tool.toml files from workspace repos to website. Should:

1. Read website repo path from [website] config section
2. Walk workspace repos looking for tool.toml
3. Parse and validate against schema (govnr/examples/tool.toml)
4. Generate/update tool pages in website repo (config: toolz_dir)
5. Update toolz/index.js with tools array
6. Copy media files (icon, screenshot) to public/ (config: public_dir)
7. Be idempotent - only update if content changed
8. Support --commit flag to auto-commit changes
9. Support localized fields (tagline_de, description_de, etc.)

title: byt memory should auto-detect repo from cwd git remote, not just catalog
description: When running 'byt memory add' from ~/byteowlz/octo, it says 'At workspace root or outside workspace, using govnr store' even though octo is a valid git repo in the byteowlz workspace. byt should: 1) Check if cwd is inside a git repo, 2) Extract repo name from git remote or directory name, 3) Use that as the store name (creating if needed). Currently it only checks the catalog, which may not be up to date.

title: Add explicit repo registration: byt catalog add / byt project add
Add explicit repo registration: byt catalog add / byt project add
description:
## Goal

Allow explicit registration of a new repo instead of (or alongside) the full-scan `byt catalog refresh`. Motivation: created `forgejo/wismut/bench` and there was no way to register it directly — only a whole-fleet refresh, and catalog output gives no confirmation that a specific new repo was picked up.

## Proposed UX

```bash
byt catalog add <path>          # register repo at path (validates: git repo, remote, AGENTS.md/justfile/.trx presence)
byt catalog add <path> --machine <name>   # override machine label (default: current)
byt project add                 # alias, if "project" is the user-facing noun
byt catalog remove <name>       # symmetric removal
```

## Notes

- `catalog add` should print the resulting catalog entry (name, machine, remote, missing-requirement warnings).
- Keep `refresh` as the reconciliation path; `add` is the targeted, scriptable one for agents (today's flow would be: create repo -> `byt catalog add` -> done, no ambiguity).
- Machine-mismatch handling: if path is on a shared mount, record explicitly rather than guessing.

## Acceptance

- `byt catalog add ~/byteowlz/bench` registers the new repo and prints its entry.
- Invalid path / non-git dir -> clear error, no catalog mutation.
- `catalog list` shows the added repo immediately.

(landed before this issue was filed). Verified end-to-end against the real
source repo:

- `byt design-system sync --repo oqto_refactor` → fetches `byteowlz/design-system@v0.1.0`

- **D1 confirmed:** syncs `src/` only — `dist/` and `node_modules/` correctly
  absent (dist is gitignored build artifact).

  - `status` → `[behind (pinned v0.1.0 -> latest v0.1.0)]` when upstream advances
  - `status` → `[diverged (local edits since sync; pinned v0.1.0)]` when locals

  `--repo` / `--ref` / `--build` flags, global `--dry-run`.
- Config model matches spec: global `DesignSystemConfig` defaults +
  per-consumer `design-system.toml` manifest (source/ref/impl/path/build_cmd).

Design-system repo tagged `v0.1.0` (first pinned ref). oqto manifest at

title: byt hooks install: pull shared git hooks from byteowlz/githooks (always-current, cross-machine)
description:
Add `byt hooks install` / status / update — install the shared byteowlz git hooks by pulling from byteowlz/githooks into a machine cache, so hooks always come from the repo (no drift) and resolve cross-machine.

RATIONALE
- byteowlz/githooks (canonical) now holds the schema-versioning pre-commit guard (primary, agent-friendly: validates staged *.schema.json) + a pre-push egress gate (push-range guard + planned gitleaks secret scan). Templates vendor a committed .githooks/ as OFFLINE fallback; byt is the ONLINE always-current path.
- Vendored committed copies drift; an absolute core.hooksPath breaks cross-machine. byt hooks install solves both: pull latest from the repo into ~/.cache/byteowlz/hooks, then git config core.hooksPath <cache>/hooks (per-repo, machine-local).

DESIGN
1. `byt hooks install [--repo <dir>]` (default cwd):
   - ensure machine cache (<XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache>/byteowlz/hooks); clone byteowlz/githooks on first run, else git pull (always current).
   - set core.hooksPath <cache>/hooks in the target repo.
   - report installed hook files + any missing optional scanner (gitleaks present?).
2. `byt hooks status [--repo <dir>]`: show core.hooksPath, hook files present, gitleaks availability.
3. `byt hooks update`: force-refresh the cache without (re)wiring a repo.
4. Graceful / non-fragile:
   - githooks unreachable -> keep last-known cache, warn (do not block).
   - no cache + unreachable -> clear error.
   - scanner binary absent -> hooks install fine; status reports missing; runtime wrapper warn-only, never wedges a push.

SCOPE NOTES
- Command dispatch lives alongside existing secrets/lint subcommands in src/main.rs (clap Subcommand enum + try_main match).
- Cache dir honors XDG_CACHE_HOME (byteowlz config conventions).
- Prefer git-over-https to byteowlz/githooks; allow BYT_HOOKS_SOURCE override for forks/offline.

POSITIVE-OUTCOME PROOF (agent must run and show results)
1. cargo build + clippy + tests pass; new commands appear in `byt --help` / `byt hooks --help`.
2. On a scratch repo: `byt hooks install` sets core.hooksPath to the cache and copies current files (pre-commit, pre-push, schema-guard); a second run after the source repo changes picks up the change (proves always-pull).
3. `byt hooks status` shows gitleaks presence and the wired path.
4. A staged bad *.schema.json (missing version) is BLOCKED by the installed pre-commit; a valid one passes (proves the installed hooks actually run).
5. With the source unreachable and a cache present, install warns and keeps hooks working.

RELATED
- byteowlz/githooks (canonical hook source; this session). byteowlz/templates vendored fallback. Companion trx: dpty/gvnr schema work (schemas.json versioning + dpty-recipe/dpty-capability/gvnr-dpty-wire).

title: scaffolded rust-workspace repos inherit wrong crate name (rust_core) — template must parameterize crate namespace
description:
BUG: scaffolded rust-workspace repos carry wrong crate name (rust_core / rust-api / rust-cli / rust-tui / rust-mcp) — win more than a mechanical fix.

OBSERVED
- byteowlz/gvnr was scaffolded from the rust-workspace template; its crates kept the template's placeholder crate names: crates import `rust_core::{AppConfig,AppPaths}` while Cargo.toml deps declare `gvnr-core`. The workspace does not compile until every `rust_core` import is renamed to the real crate name. (Mechanical fix is being done in the gvnr lane; THIS bug tracks the durable root cause.)

ROOT CAUSE
- Byteowlz/templates/rust-workspace hardcodes the crate namespace: crates/ are named rust-core, rust-api, rust-cli, rust-tui, rust-mcp and reference each other as rust_core everywhere (32 refs). There is NO {{project_name}}/crate-name substitution in the template. So every repo created from it inherits the placeholder crate name and breaks on first build.

EXPECTED
- Templates must parameterize the crate namespace: `byt new`/scaffolding substitutes the project's crate name (e.g. gvnr-core, gvnr-api, gvnr-cli) at scaffold time, producing a compliant, immediately-buildable workspace. No hardcoded `rust_*` crate names in a generated repo.

SCOPE
1. Rust-workspace (and rust-cli?) template: derive crate names from the project name (project_name -> {project}[-core|-api|-cli|-tui|-mcp]); rename crates/ dirs + the 32 `rust_core`/`rust-*` refs.
2. byt new scaffolding: pass the project name into template rendering for crate naming; verify a generated repo builds (cargo build) out of the box.
3. Add a positive-outcome check: scaffold gvnr-style workspace -> cargo build passes with correct crate names; assert no `rust_core`/`rust-*` placeholder survives in generated output.
4. Consider a lint/check in templates CI that generated samples contain no `rust_` placeholder.

RELATED
- byteowlz/gvnr lane (gvnr-bdbj) is doing the one-off mechanical fix; it is NOT the fix for this bug.
- byteowlz/templates (canonical), byt-scaffolding (this repo).

title: byt audit + lift: converge older repos to template parity (guardrails, lints, hooks, gitattributes, CI)
description:
EPIC: `byt audit` / `byt lift` — converge older repos to template parity (guardrails, lints, hooks, gitattributes, CI).

WHY
- byteowlz/templates defines the expected shape for new repos (hooks, lints, gitattributes merge=union, CI gates, justfile recipes, config schema, AGENTS.md discipline). Older repos predate them and drift (e.g. gvnr scaffolded with stale rust_core crate name = byt-0vg5; most repos lack .githooks = byt-m8gj). We keep bolting on one-off fixes; this makes convergence one coherent capability.

DESIGN
1. `byt audit [repo]` — infer flavor (rust-workspace/rust-cli/python-cli/go-cli from Cargo.toml/pyproject.toml/go.mod). Compare repo state against the flavor's EXPECTED manifest, classifying each item:
   - standard: expected in every byteowlz repo (githooks+setup-hooks, .gitattributes merge=union for trx, .trx hygiene)
   - flavor: expected for this language (clippy/fmt/+ast-grep guardrails, golangci-lint, ruff/uv; release workflow; config schema + validation)
   - drifted: present but != expected (stale lint config, missing CI quality gate, old crate names)
   - custom: repo-specific -> NEVER touched
   Emit a categorized, reviewable diff (missing / drifted / unknown adds).
2. `byt lift [repo] [--categories=guardrails,lints,hooks,gitattributes,ci,justfile,config-schema] [--dry-run] [--yes]` — apply the delta:
   - drop-in files that don't exist; three-way-merge files that exist and differ; on conflict report-rather-than-clobber.
   - idempotent; dry-run is the default; apply lands as a reviewable commit.
3. Gradation not big-bang: audit first, then per-category staged lifts. A mature repo's divergent CI/guardrails stay `custom` and are preserved (trust-but-verify; lift converges, never takes over).
4. Reuses machinery: `byt hooks install` = lift's hooks category (byt-m8gj); cratename/tooling fix = lift's tooling category (byt-0vg5). Centralizes the TEMPLATE-as-source-of-truth expectation behind one command surface.

POSITIVE-OUTCOME PROOF (agent must run and show results)
1. cargo build + clippy + tests pass; `byt audit --help`/`byt lift --help` render.
2. On a deliberately stripped test repo (no .githooks, no .gitattributes merge, no lint config), `byt audit` flags the missing standard/flavor items by category, and `byt lift --categories=hooks,gitattributes --dry-run` shows exactly the files it would drop in (matches byt hooks install output for the hooks category).
3. On a repo with a drifted lint config (e.g. stale clippy level / old CI gate), lift reports DRIFTED and three-way-merges or reports-on-conflict, and NEVER clobbers a `custom` file.
4. Idempotency: running lift twice yields no further changes.
5. Root-cause tie: scaffolding a rust-workspace repo (byt-0vg5) then `byt audit` shows the correct crate-name expectation vs scaffolded output.

RELATED / DEPENDS
- byt-m8gj (hooks install), byt-0vg5 (crate-name/tooling), byteowlz/templates (canonical expectation source), byteowlz/githooks.
- Child issues to be filed: expectation-manifest format; audit engine; lift/apply engine; per-flavor recipes.
